sections.title: What a clothes shop sells
sections.content: A *ruhabolt* is a clothes shop: *ruha* (clothes) and *bolt* (shop). It sells *ing* (shirt), *póló* (T-shirt), *nadrág* (trousers), *kabát* (coat) and *cipő* (shoe). To say you are buying something, use *veszek*. The thing is the object, so it takes *-t*: *Egy inget veszek.* (I am buying a shirt.)

sections.title: Which ending?
sections.content: A word that ends in a long vowel just takes *-t* (*póló → pólót*, *cipő → cipőt*). After a consonant a linking vowel comes first: *-ot* after back vowels (*nadrágot*, *kabátot*, *ruhaboltot*) and *-et* after front vowels (*inget*).

items.english: I would like a pair of trousers.

sections.content: *Veszek* goes with *egy* or no article, as *kérek* does: *Egy inget veszek.* For one particular thing you know, the verb changes, and you will use it in lesson 123.
